findings.claim: This repository still builds the limit message as `You can only add up to ${max - existing} more.` with no guard, so users at the limit see "up to 0 more" and users over the limit see a negative number.
This repository has the same unguarded message-construction pattern, producing "up to 0 more" or a negative remaining count instead of the corrected wording applied elsewhere.
This e2e test still asserts the old "…up to 0 more." text, so it would need updating once the same fix is applied to the address-book repositories.

No shared helper exists for building this limit message, so the same string-construction logic is duplicated across the three repositories; extracting it into one small shared helper would prevent the fix from being applied inconsistently.

The new test only covers the remaining === 0 case; there is no test for existing > max (the case that previously produced "add up to -N more"), so that branch of the guard is unverified even though the same > 0 check handles it.
The limit check reads the current count and performs the insert as two separate, non-atomic operations, so two concurrent requests could both pass the check and together exceed the configured limit.
